summary: The note explains how blockchain, a distributed ledger technology, helps small and medium enterprises (SMEs) improve transparency, security, payment efficiency and regulatory compliance. It gives examples such as Mercer & Sons, Secure Ledger Inc. and GreenTech Innovations, plus expert comments on smart contracts and audits. It also covers adoption challenges like high initial costs and a steep learning curve, and concludes that SME adoption is poised for substantial growth.
one_line: Blockchain can give SMEs greater transparency, security, efficiency and easier compliance, though cost and learning curves hinder adoption.
key_facts: Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology that stores data globally on thousands of servers, making transactions independently verifiable and virtually incorruptible.
Blockchain gained initial prominence as the backbone of cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, but its business uses extend beyond digital currencies.
On November 12, 2023, a report by the SME Innovation Council highlighted blockchain's effectiveness in boosting transparency.
Retail SME Mercer & Sons used blockchain to track its supply chain, letting customers verify product origin and quality in real-time.
Tech entrepreneur Jane Smith said in a webinar on October 15, 2023 that smart contracts could save SMEs thousands in legal fees and remove the need for intermediaries.
Smart contracts are self-executing contracts with terms written directly into code, and are tamper-proof and automatically enforceable.

Secure Ledger Inc. implemented a blockchain solution for customer data management on January 2, 2024; CEO Michael Rodriguez reported a drastic reduction in attempted security breaches and an influx of interested clients.

In a September 15, 2023 interview, Allison Chen, CFO of GreenTech Innovations, said blockchain cut transaction costs and clearing time with international suppliers, enabling near-instantaneous transactions that previously could take several days through a bank.
At a summit on blockchain in SMEs on February 20, 2024, legal expert Harold Jennings said blockchain's transparency lets SMEs prove compliance effortlessly through seamless regulator audits.
Blockchain's immutable record-keeping gives SMEs an unalterable data history needed for auditing and compliance.
Adoption challenges include a high initial implementation cost and a steep learning curve for employees.
Growing numbers of service providers and SME-focused education programs and platforms are helping address adoption challenges.
Blockchain lets SMEs avoid the centralization risks of conventional databases because its distributed nature makes data less vulnerable to hacking and fraud.
